TryModifyRewards.maps_to: modify_combat_rewards (sts2_rl/relics/black_star.py:15-23) -- appends the payload-less RelicReward to an ELITE screen and offers it through RunState.offer_relic
TryModifyRewards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the take-or-skip seam exists and this site uses it. `RunState.offer_relic` (sts2_rl/run.py:475-496) and `RunState.offer_potion` (sts2_rl/run.py:498-506) are the port of RewardsCmd.OfferCustom's declinable RelicReward / PotionReward: they consult `run.reward_selector` (the driver surfaces it as a REWARD_RELIC / REWARD_POTION decision) and only call add_relic / add_potion on a take, so a declined relic never runs its AfterObtained -- RelicReward.OnSelect (RelicReward.cs:109-115) is the only path to RelicCmd.Obtain. sts2_rl/relics/black_star.py now pulls the relic and calls `run.offer_relic(relic)`. WAS: the port called run.add_relic itself, so the player could not decline and the relic's own after_obtained fired regardless.

guards.what: N1: `player != base.Owner` and the null-room bail (BlackStar.cs:9-16)
guards.rationale: The `player != base.Owner` / `shuffler == base.Owner` / `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Owner` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player. The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState), so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

guards.what: N2: the relic is granted at SCREEN-GENERATION time in the sim and at TAKE time in C#, so a run that never opens the screen differs
guards.rationale: The sim generates a reward screen only when a combat actually ends in victory, and every generated screen is resolved, so there is no path where the relic is pulled and then not granted. The one consumer that could tell the difference -- the conformance runner's relic parity check -- compares the relic LIST after the screen resolves, by which time both codebases agree.
